title: Box Plot
intent: Create grouped boxes, medians, whiskers, and optional outliers from quantitative observations.
useWhen: Use this recipe when robust distribution summaries and outliers should be compared across groups.
avoidWhen: Avoid this recipe when the complete distribution shape or individual observations must remain visible.
prerequisites: Provide immutable row objects containing every field named by the selected actions and example program.
Use explicit public resource identifiers whenever current program state contains more than one compatible candidate.

inputs.name: values
inputs.description: An array of plain row objects containing the fields required by this task.

inputs.name: options
inputs.description: Task-specific field names, resource identifiers, and supported visual or statistical choices.

outcomes: Create grouped boxes, medians, whiskers, and optional outliers from quantitative observations.

steps.instruction: Create the data, marks, encodings, and owned resources required before authoring the box plot result.
Apply the primary action that produces the recognizable box plot result or workflow.
Apply color after the box-plot facade and target the stable box-plot owner explicitly.
Use the focused lifecycle actions only after their owned box plot resources exist and are uniquely targeted.

alternatives.when: Choose a neighboring recipe when its stated result and data roles match the requested chart more directly.
alternatives.instruction: Prefer one complete domain facade or task recipe before composing lower-level actions manually.

pitfalls.problem: The createBoxPlot action does not accept a color option even when categories should use distinct fills.
pitfalls.fix: Call encodeColor after createBoxPlot with target boxPlot, the categorical field, and nominal fieldType.

pitfalls.problem: Coloring boxes by the same category shown on an axis can create a redundant legend.
pitfalls.fix: Set guides.legend to false in createBoxPlot or manage the legend explicitly through guide lifecycle actions.

pitfalls.problem: A copied box-plot recipe with an implicit Canvas leaves its dimensions and guide space unresolved.
pitfalls.fix: Keep the example's explicit Canvas width, height, and margins when adapting fields or returning the program to a host renderer.

pitfalls.problem: Implicit targeting fails when several compatible datasets, marks, scales, guides, or owners exist in the same program.
pitfalls.fix: Pass the exact public identifier named by the action signature instead of relying on first-resource selection.
